title: A Clean Slate for Offline Reinforcement Learning

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract / Section 4.1 (training speedup claim: '131.5× and 74.8× against OfflineRL-Kit and CORL')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract and Section 4.1 claim average speedups of 131.5x vs OfflineRL-Kit and 74.8x vs CORL. However, Appendix F Table 2 provides the raw training times used to compute these speedups. Computing the per-algorithm ratios from Table 2 (e.g., BC: 19.8/1.7≈11.6x, TD3-BC: 56.1/3.1≈18.1x, IQL: 79.7/4.0≈19.9x, SAC-N: 107.5/7.7≈14.0x, CQL: 203.9/9.8≈20.8x, EDAC: 127.1/20.8≈6.1x, MOPO: 168.1/14.0≈12.0x, COMBO: 289.6/22.0≈13.2x) and averaging gives roughly 14.5x for OfflineRL-Kit, not 131.5x. The corresponding CORL-based average is roughly 11x-13x, not 74.8x. These headline numbers are not supported by the underlying data in Table 2.

predicted_errors.error_location: Figure 5 ('Unifloral Speedup Over Other Implementations') vs Appendix F, Table 2
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Figure 5 reports ReBRAC speedup of 8x and CQL speedup of 14x. However, Table 2 shows ReBRAC training times of 8.7 min (CORL) vs 6.8 min (Unifloral), a ratio of only ~1.28x, not 8x (no OfflineRL-Kit time is even reported for ReBRAC). Similarly, CQL times are 203.9 min (OfflineRL-Kit) / 9.8 min (Unifloral) ≈ 20.8x, or 180.3/9.8≈18.4x (CORL), neither matching the reported 14x. BC's reported 16x speedup similarly doesn't match computed ratios of ~8.8x–11.6x from Table 2. These two tables present conflicting speedup figures for the same comparisons.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5.1 (TD3-AWR evaluation) vs Figure 6 / Appendix J (Figure 14)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states: 'TD3-AWR outperforms ReBRAC on several datasets but underperforms or matches it on others, such as pen-human and kitchen-mixed.' However, the pen-human-v1 panel in Figure 6 and the corresponding panel in Appendix J (Figure 14) show TD3-AWR and IQL reaching ~65-70 while ReBRAC reaches only ~40 — i.e., TD3-AWR clearly outperforms, not underperforms or merely matches, ReBRAC on pen-human.

The text first states 'Figure 7 shows how MoBRAC outperforms other model-based algorithms for all datasets, except for MOPO in maze2d-large-v1' (implying MoBRAC wins on 8 of 9 datasets), but then states 'MoBRAC outperforms the other model-based methods in 6 out of 9 datasets and is tied with MOPO for 3 others' (implying only 6 wins and 3 ties, with no losses). These two claims about MoBRAC's relative performance are mutually inconsistent (8 wins/1 loss vs 6 wins/3 ties/0 losses).

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.2 (unified actor loss) vs Appendix I.1 Eq. (7) and I.2 Eq. (8)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 4.2 defines the unified actor loss as 'L_actor = β_q·L_q + β_BC·L_BC − β_H·H(π(·|s_t)) + β_div·L_div + β_dyn·L_dyn', including a critic diversity term β_div·L_div as part of the actor objective. However, Appendix I.1 Eq. (7) explicitly places the diversity loss term (from EDAC) inside the critic loss, not the actor loss, and Appendix I.2 Eq. (8), which is presented as the fully detailed unified actor loss, omits both the β_div·L_div and β_dyn·L_dyn terms entirely. The main text and appendix equations for the same loss are therefore inconsistent with each other.

The paper claims 'Our evaluation procedure avoids these constraints by requiring no reference policies or extra hyperparameters' (repeated in Appendix L.1: '...a procedure that eliminates the need for reference policies or additional hyperparameters'). However, the proposed evaluation procedure explicitly relies on a UCB bandit algorithm (Section 3.2), which itself introduces hyperparameters (e.g., exploration coefficient, number of arms K, number of pulls N, number of bootstrap repetitions B), contradicting the claim of requiring 'no extra hyperparameters'.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5.2 ('all considered methods using SAC-N or CQL (Figure 5)')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text cites 'Figure 5' as evidence that 'all considered methods [are] using SAC-N or CQL' as policy optimizers in model-based offline RL. However, Figure 5 ('Unifloral Speedup Over Other Implementations') is a table of training speedups, not a description of which policy optimizer each model-based algorithm uses. This figure does not support or contain the claim being attributed to it.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.2 'Recommended Datasets' vs Section 3.3, Figure 3, Appendix B (Figure 8), Appendix J/K
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 3.2 recommends evaluation on exactly 8 datasets: hopper-medium-v2, halfcheetah-medium-expert-v2, walker2d-medium-replay-v2, pen-human-v1, pen-cloned-v1, pen-expert-v1, kitchen-mixed-v0, and maze2d-large-v1. However, the actual evaluation used throughout the paper (Section 3.3's '9 datasets', Appendix B's 3x3 grid, and the dataset lists in Appendices J/K) includes a 9th dataset, antmaze-large-diverse-v2, that is never mentioned in the 'Recommended Datasets' list, creating an inconsistency between the stated protocol and the one actually used.

Equation (5) defines 'v̂_{t+1} = v_{t+1} + α_BC·(ã_{t+1} − a_{t+1}) + α_H·H(π(·|s_{t+1}))'. Here (ã_{t+1} − a_{t+1}) is a difference between two action vectors (which are multi-dimensional for continuous-control tasks), yet it is added directly to the scalar value target v_{t+1} with only a scalar coefficient α_BC, with no norm or squared-distance operation applied. This is dimensionally inconsistent and contrasts with the squared-distance/log-probability formulation used for the equivalent behavior-cloning term in Eq. (10).

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.1 ('BC, TD3-BC, ReBRAC, IQL, SAC-N, LB-SAC, EDAC, CQL, DT') and Figure 10a genealogy
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: LB-SAC is listed as one of the implemented model-free algorithms in Section 4.1 and appears in the algorithm genealogy (Figure 10a: 'SAC-N → LB-SAC, EDAC, MOPO, CQL'), but it is never described in Appendix A (Algorithm Implementations in Unifloral), never evaluated in Table 3, Figure 3/8, or included in the speedup comparisons (Figure 5, Table 2). A method claimed to be implemented is absent from all subsequent descriptions and results.
